tokyo_chinya.price_note: ⚠ THE PRICES BELOW ARE MAIL-ORDER, NOT RESTAURANT PRICES, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE CAVEAT. The page at chinya.co.jp/menu/ turns out to be the shop’s ONLINE SHOP — raw sukiyaki meat sets, miso-cured meat and tsukudani sold by weight for delivery — rather than the dining-room board. No in-restaurant dish, course or price is published anywhere on the site that was read. The items are recorded because they are real, priced and first-party, and because their composition is informative; they are not what you would be served at a table. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT THE PRODUCT NAMES ESTABLISH FOR A COELIAC, AND IT IS THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS AT ANY SUKIYAKI HOUSE: every meat set is sold 割下付き — WITH WARISHITA, the sukiyaki cooking liquid, which is soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Sukiyaki is not meat with a sauce on the side; the warishita is the medium the beef is cooked in, so there is no version of the dish without it unless the kitchen will do a salt-and-oil 関西風 preparation, which nothing here mentions. Sukiyaki is also conventionally dipped in raw EGG. ⚠ AND THE SET PRODUCTS NAME THEIR OWN VEGETABLES: ザク (the vegetable mix), 白滝 (shirataki, konjac noodles — plant and wheat-free, unlike every other noodle in this dataset) and 焼き豆腐 (grilled tofu). Those three are the parts of a sukiyaki a plant-eater could in principle eat, and they arrive in a pan of soy-based beef stock.
